column3: “Cried a cry loud and bitter” is rendered “wailed loudly and bitterly.”
“It was spread as a bed by many” is rendered “many lay on sackcloth and ashes.”
“Agonized exceedingly” is rendered “writhed in great anguish.”
“Whom he had made stand before her” is rendered “whom the king had appointed to attend her.” NASB supplies “to go.”
“The open place of the city” is rendered “the city square.”
“To seek favor to him” is rendered “to implore his favor.”
“Extends” is rendered “holds out.” NASB supplies “for these.”
“Imagine in yourself” is rendered “imagine”; NASB supplies “any more than.”
“Certainly keep quiet” is rendered “remain silent,” and “reached the queenhood” as “attained royalty.” NASB supplies “not.”
“Fast on me” is rendered “fast for me.” “Just as I have perished, I have perished” is rendered “if I perish, I perish.”
